clue.text: Alliance in Zagreb locale

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of letters across the words Zagreb locale

explanation.surface: A political alliance seems to be forming somewhere in the Croatian capital.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloc is a group of nations or parties combined for a common purpose.

clue.text: Dancing allowed by graduate student?

parts.note: BA is a Bachelor of Arts, a graduate
L for learner, as on a learner driver's plate
allowed means let

explanation.surface: A graduate student gets permission to take up dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' just places LET beside BA and L; L is the learner's letter on British driving plates.
explanation.definitionFit: Ballet is a classical form of theatrical dance, so it names dancing as an art.

clue.text: Reform Act with anagram for John's charter?

indicators.note: to reform something is to reshape it, so the letters of act and anagram are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bill to reform an act, with a playful anagram attached, poses as a royal charter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reform Act' looks like the 1832 parliamentary Reform Act; 'Reform' is really the anagram signal acting on ACT and ANAGRAM together.
explanation.definitionFit: Magna Carta was the charter King John sealed at Runnymede in 1215, hence John's charter.

clue.text: Refuge from year in a favela?

indicators.note: the letter for year is placed in the middle of a plus the shanty-town word

parts.note: a favela is a Brazilian shanty town, a slum

explanation.surface: Someone seeks shelter from a year spent living in a Brazilian shanty town.
explanation.definitionFit: Asylum is protection or shelter granted to someone fleeing danger, a place of safety.

clue.text: Fellow with the cheek to oust last bureaucrat

parts.note: a fellow is a man

indicators.note: ousting the final letter means the boldness word loses its last letter

parts.note: cheek, boldness, is daring

explanation.surface: A cheeky fellow tries to throw out the last official in the office.
explanation.definitionFit: A mandarin is a senior civil servant, after the high officials of imperial China.

clue.text: Donkey's stealing heart from Governess Grey?

indicators.note: taking away the heart means the central letter of the governess's name is removed

parts.note: Agnes Grey is the governess heroine of Anne Brontë's novel of that name

explanation.surface: Someone or something steals the heart of a prim Victorian governess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Donkey's' is short for 'donkey's years', British slang for a very long time.
explanation.definitionFit: Donkey's years is an idiom for a very long time, the same as saying for ages.

clue.text: Old PM is with artist entering exotic food shop

indicators.note: entering means is and the artist go into the shop word

parts.note: a deli, or delicatessen, sells fine and foreign foods
taken as written
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: An elderly prime minister turns up with a painter at a fancy delicatessen.
explanation.definitionFit: Benjamin Disraeli was Britain's Conservative prime minister in 1868 and again from 1874 to 1880.

clue.text: Something stale in the fridge? That's unlucky

definitions.meaning: a piece of cheese gone hard with age, read literally
a British expression of sympathy, often ironic, for bad luck

explanation.surface: Finding dried-up leftovers in the fridge prompts a rueful comment.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard cheese is British slang meaning tough luck, so it says that's unlucky; literally it is cheese gone dry.

clue.text: Wool supplier completely backed by mother

indicators.note: backed means the word for completely is read backwards

parts.note: completely means all
ma is mother

explanation.surface: A wool supplier receives full backing from mother.
explanation.definitionFit: The llama is a South American animal whose fleece is spun into wool.

clue.text: Girl has an untidy place that's idyllic

indicators.note: something untidy is messed up, so the letters of girl has an are jumbled

explanation.surface: A girl has a messy room, which is hardly paradise.
explanation.definitionFit: Shangri-La, from James Hilton's Lost Horizon, is an imaginary earthly paradise.

clue.text: Mustard? You might pick up the seed!

indicators.note: to pick up is to hear, so the seed word is taken as heard spoken

parts.note: a kernel is the seed inside a nut or fruit

explanation.surface: A cook reaching for mustard is told to collect the seed as well.
explanation.walkthrough: Mustard seed tempts the reader, but Mustard is the Cluedo suspect; the answer and KERNEL are pronounced alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Colonel Mustard is one of the suspects in the board game Cluedo (Clue in North America).

clue.text: Wanted something done about Elton's title?

indicators.note: about means the action word goes around the knight's title

parts.note: a deed is something done
Elton John is a knight, so his title is Sir

explanation.surface: A fan wants something done about Elton John's honour.
explanation.definitionFit: Desired is a past form of desire, the same as wanted.

clue.text: An unknown detective finding Montezuma?

parts.note: an gives A
Z is an algebraic unknown
tec is short for detective

explanation.surface: A mystery detective goes looking for an ancient emperor.
explanation.definitionFit: Montezuma was the Aztec emperor when the Spanish conquistadors arrived; the question mark marks him as an example.

clue.text: Article by Signora Peron, born in Chile, within reach

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: in means Eva and the born letter go inside the name of the country

parts.note: taken as written
Eva Perón, Argentina's first lady

explanation.surface: An article about Eva Perón being born in Chile seems within reach.
explanation.definitionFit: Achievable means attainable, something one can reach or accomplish.

clue.text: Tool used in demonstration in city

indicators.note: used in means the tool goes inside the protest word

parts.note: a march is a protest demonstration
a rake is a garden tool

explanation.surface: A garden tool gets brandished at a protest in town.
explanation.definitionFit: Marrakech is a major city of Morocco.

clue.text: Run from politician going after a Democrat

indicators.note: going after means the politician comes behind a and the Democrat letter

parts.note: a minister is a politician in government

explanation.surface: A minister chases a Democrat, perhaps to run from them.
explanation.definitionFit: To administer an organisation is to manage or run it.

clue.text: Pious type, one with seat in Ireland, unified states once

parts.note: pious means holy
roman is the upright typeface

indicators.note: in means the parliamentarian goes inside the name for Ireland

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name for Ireland
an MP holds a seat in Parliament

explanation.surface: A devout person and a politician holding an Irish seat sound like a union of nations.
explanation.definitionFit: The Holy Roman Empire was a historical union of central European territories that lasted until 1806.

clue.text: Greatly upset about hot, sleepy condition

indicators.note: about means the jumbled letters go around the letter for hot
upset means the letters of greatly are knocked into a new order

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: Someone is badly upset at being too hot and drowsy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' makes LETARGY from GREATLY, and 'about' puts that round H.
explanation.definitionFit: Lethargy is a state of sluggishness and drowsy lack of energy.

clue.text: Support son immersed in sea and Scots river

indicators.note: immersed in means the son letter is dipped inside the sea and river words together

parts.note: the main is a literary word for the open sea
the Tay is Scotland's longest river

explanation.surface: A father holds up his son, who is swimming in the sea and a Scottish river.
explanation.definitionFit: A mainstay is a chief support, originally a stay supporting a ship's mainmast.

clue.text: Send back additional edit for revision

parts.note: additional means extra

indicators.note: something up for revision gets reworked, so the letters of edit are rearranged

explanation.surface: An editor sends a manuscript back for one more round of edits.
explanation.definitionFit: To extradite is to hand a suspect over to the country where they are wanted.

clue.text: My robe redesigned in developmental stage

indicators.note: something redesigned is remade, so the letters of my robe are reordered

explanation.surface: A tailor reworks a robe that is still being developed.
explanation.definitionFit: An embryo is an organism at its earliest stage of growth, and figuratively anything just beginning.

clue.text: Apostate finally accepted by respectable relative

indicators.note: being accepted by means the chosen letter is taken into the respectable word

parts.note: nice in the sense of proper, respectable

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of apostate

explanation.surface: A respectable family finally welcomes back a member who had lapsed from the faith.
explanation.definitionFit: A niece is the daughter of one's brother or sister, a family relative.

clue.text: Prophet having Sheila converted

indicators.note: converted means changed in form, so the letters of Sheila are reordered

explanation.surface: A prophet wins over a woman named Sheila to his faith.
explanation.definitionFit: Elisha was the Old Testament prophet who succeeded Elijah.

clue.text: Flummoxed with income less than outlay?

definitions.meaning: flummoxed means puzzled, not knowing what to do
a business whose income is below its outlay trades ...

explanation.surface: Someone is baffled to find they are spending more than they earn.
explanation.definitionFit: At a loss is an idiom for bewildered, and literally describes trading in deficit.

clue.text: Nothing in which to dip quill? Pen's sound!

parts.note: O is the round figure nought, nothing
a quill pen is dipped in ink

explanation.surface: A writer with no ink for the quill hears the scratch of the pen.
explanation.walkthrough: The writing picture misleads: the pen here is a pigpen.
explanation.definitionFit: Oink is the grunt of a pig, the animal kept in a pen.

clue.text: French good to guard Italian wine in fortress

indicators.note: guarding means the French word goes around the wine, keeping it safe

parts.note: bon is French for good
Asti is a sparkling wine from Piedmont

explanation.surface: A good Frenchman keeps watch over Italian wine stored in a fortress.
explanation.definitionFit: A bastion is a projecting part of a fortification, and by extension a stronghold.

clue.text: Fiddling emperor in north-east or heading north

indicators.note: in a down answer heading north means or is read upwards, backwards

explanation.surface: An emperor fiddles somewhere in the north-east, or heads north.
explanation.definitionFit: Nero is the Roman emperor said to have fiddled while Rome burned.

clue.text: Renowned stage close by a railway

parts.note: a leg is a stage of a journey
a close is an end

explanation.surface: A famous journey stage finishes beside a railway line.
explanation.definitionFit: Legendary means famed, so celebrated as to be the stuff of legend.

clue.text: Old number three fouled

indicators.note: fouled means tangled up, so the letters of three are jumbled

explanation.surface: An old player wearing the number three committed a foul.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' is not a figure but something that numbs.
explanation.definitionFit: Ether was an early anaesthetic, a numbing agent now out of use.
